problems.label: Disorganization, lateness and unfinished tasks at work and home
definitions: Misses deadlines or appointments at least weekly and loses important items several times a month.
Starts tasks but leaves many unfinished, and puts off tasks until the last minute.
Reports conflict with a partner, employer or family about forgotten tasks or lateness.
longTermGoals: The client uses a simple, reliable system for time and tasks, finishes what matters most and feels more in control of daily life.

shortTermObjectives.text: By session 2, set up one calendar and one task list, and check them every morning on at least 5 days a week for 4 weeks.
Each week, break the 3 most important tasks into first steps and complete at least 2 of them on time.
Use timed work blocks of 15 to 25 minutes at least 4 times a week and log how much was completed.
Within 4 weeks, attend an evaluation with a prescriber experienced in adult ADHD, if the client wishes to consider medication.
Practice a 5-minute attention exercise at least 4 days a week for 4 weeks and rate focus before and after.
Complete the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and every 4 weeks to track low mood and worry alongside attention goals.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit.
